relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: David's kingdom expands into Philistine cities through conquest.
Moab is defeated and placed under tribute.
Hadadezer is struck as competing control reaches toward the Euphrates.
Soldiers, chariots, and horses become captured assets; most horses are deliberately disabled.
Twenty-two thousand Arameans die while aiding their ally.
Garrisons and tribute establish occupation, interpreted as Divine victory.
Gold shields move from defeated servants into Jerusalem.
Bronze stripped from conquered cities later becomes temple architecture.
Tou hears that his enemy Hadadezer has fallen.
Diplomacy follows victory with congratulations and precious metals.
Plunder from many peoples is dedicated as sacred wealth.
Eighteen thousand Edomites die under Abishai.
Edom receives garrisons and forced service while the narrator repeats Divine victory.
David is praised for justice and righteousness inside an empire built through these campaigns.
Joab and Jehoshaphat manage army and royal memory.
Priests and scribe organize sacred and administrative power.
Benaiah commands elite troops while David's sons occupy high office.

contemplative_note: The chapter calls David's rule just while cataloging conquered cities, tribute, garrisons, mutilated horses, mass death, and sacred objects made from plunder. The tension must remain. Justice is not established by what the royal archive calls it, but by what occupied people, workers, animals, and bereaved families experience.
